technical_and_design_decisions: All modules (source, sink, REST API) will be built on the Spring XD platform to align with requirements for cluster deployment and stream processing.
The Kafka source module will use the Spring for Apache Kafka simple consumer API (not the high-level consumer) to meet the requirement for deterministic offset and partition management.

The mass ingest solution (U1) will leverage existing, production-ready Spring XD database source and HDFS/HAWQ/GPDB sink modules with configuration-based customization, rather than building custom ingest logic from scratch.

The perf-meter sink will calculate message rate as the number of messages processed since the last log event divided by the elapsed time (in seconds) between log events, to provide accurate throughput metrics.
The custom module deployment REST API will store uploaded uber-jar modules in a shared cluster-accessible filesystem for simplicity, as no specific persistence requirement is specified.
Test coverage will use JUnit 5 and Spring Test frameworks, with integration tests running against an embedded Kafka instance and local Spring XD singlenode for CI compatibility.
The generator source module will generate payloads using repeated ASCII 'x' characters to achieve the specified message size, for simplicity and deterministic output.
assumptions: A local development environment with Java 17+, Maven 3.8+, Spring XD 1.3.1, and Spring for Apache Kafka 2.9+ is pre-configured for development and testing.
Access to a test Kafka cluster, test HDFS/HAWQ/GPDB instances, and test relational/NoSQL databases is available for validation of the ingest and Kafka modules.
The project's existing CI pipeline (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins) is already configured to build the project, and only test integration and execution steps need to be added.
No specific security requirements are provided for the module deployment REST API, so basic HTTP authentication will be implemented for cluster access protection.
The Spring XD singlenode environment used for U7 performance testing is configured with sufficient resources (CPU, memory) to handle the 1M message load without resource constraints.
The generator source module's payload generation does not require complex data structures, only a fixed-size byte array as specified.
